name: The five Pāśupata impurities (mala)
description: False knowledge, demerit, the cause of attachment, falling away, and the root of the paśu-state - to be abandoned; Kauṇḍinya's list: ignorance, demerit, habituation to objects, non-attainment of steadiness, lack of lordship.

name: False knowledge (mithyājñāna)
description: The first impurity; removed by the living with the teacher and learning (vāsa).

name: Demerit (adharma)
description: The second impurity; destroyed by the observance and by the transfer of demerit to revilers.

name: The cause of attachment (saktihetu)
description: The third impurity, whose removal is the third purification.

name: Falling away (cyuti)
description: The fourth impurity - the mind's slipping from Rudra; removed with its seed by constant remembrance.

name: The paśu-state (paśutva)
description: Bondage as beginningless lack of lordship; its final removal comes through connection with Maheśvara's lordship.

equivalents.note: both name the soul's root bondage; the Siddhānta's āṇava is an innate impurity, the Pāśupata paśutva lack of lordship

name: Lack of lordship (anaiśvarya)
description: Kauṇḍinya's definition of bondage and his fifth impurity.

name: Turbidity of mind (kaluṣa)
description: Mental turbidity; yoga arises only for one whose mind is unclouded; its removal is the first stage's purification.

name: Pride of birth and status (māna)
description: Pride in being a brahmin and in the honour due to householders, and pride based on wealth, kin, fame, deeds and learning; removed by dishonour.

name: Heedlessness (pramāda)
description: Inattention to what is to come and dependence; the end of suffering is reached by the vigilant.

name: The pairs of opposites (dvandva)
description: Heat and cold and the other opposites - bodily, from beings and from the gods - to be endured as cows and deer endure them; their conquest is a strength.

name: The three kinds of suffering (Pāśupata account)
description: Suffering of the self (bodily illnesses; mental states such as anger, greed, delusion, fear, despondency, envy, hatred, pride), from beings and from the gods; also womb, birth, ignorance, old age and death. Their final removal is the end of suffering.
